artworks.title: The grand stair
artworks.description: The open double stair rises three storeys over the entrance. Its underside is painted with foliage that turns into trellis work and, at the top, a sky with birds; bronze figures by the French foundry Guillaumin stand on the newel posts, and Charles Salagnad painted the pseudo-tapestry on the walls of the first flights.

artworks.title: Circassian Walnut Renaissance Revival Chimney Piece
artworks.artist: Luigi Frullini, Louis Théodore Eugène Gluck (designer)
artworks.description: A Circassian walnut Renaissance Revival chimney piece made for the Dining Room at Chateau-sur-Mer by Luigi Frullini (Italian, 1839-1897) with a faience tile surround designed by Eugène Glück (French, 1820-1898) for Theodore Deck Manufacture, Paris. The flanking cabinets of the chimney piece feature bas-relief grape cluster carvings and support a frieze with Leonine masks and projecting cherubic heads based on those of the Cantoria at the Duomo of Florence. The over-mantel shelf of Bacchic revelry consists of pendant griffons with ewers backed against a bat-winged scallop shell, against which three putti cavort. One of these putti sits clutching a grape cluster, another stands drinking from a wine cask, while the third sits atop the cask holding its cups aloft. The faience surround designed by Glück depicts a boar and stag hunt in the court of Henri IV of France. Glück favored medieval subjects and, as here, hunting scenes, some adapted from Antonio Tempesta (Italian, 1555-1630). The present hunt scene appears to be based on Tempesta's etching "Acteon a propriis canibus discerpitur" of 1606.

artworks.title: Tile Fireplace Surround
artworks.description: A fireplace surround composed of glazed earthenware tiles made by Minton Art Studios, London. Framing the fireplace in the Library of Chateau-sur-Mer, the tile frieze along the top centers on a mask of Hermes flanked by fairies and cherubs with C-scrolls, clusters of fruits and vegetables, and two dolphins along the bottom. The tiles on either side of the fireplace opening depict the female allegorical representations of Prudentia and Justice, two of the Cardinal virtues.

artworks.title: Italian Renaissance Style Library Table
artworks.dimensions: H 32.5 inches · W 86.5 inches · D 46.5 inches
artworks.description: An Italian renaissance style black walnut library table made by Luigi Frullini. The piece was created for the Chateau sur Mer library as part of an 1874-76 commission from George Peabody Wetmore. The flat rectangular top is accented with a guilloché patterned outer edge and is held up by supports in the shape of two large fully-carved owls with outstretched wings. Scrolled legs are topped with winged griffin heads and end in acanthus-sheathed lion's paws. Both ends are connected by a stretcher composed of two joined fluted acanthus and laurel leaf baluster-shaped elements.

artworks.title: Two-Tier Lacquer Tea Table
artworks.dimensions: H 28.5 inches · W 26 inches · D 15.5 inches
artworks.description: This delicate, open, two-tier table was likely supplied ca. 1876-1880 by the English cabinetmaker and furnisher, Gregory & Co. of Regent Street, London as part of the original furnishings and decoration of George Peabody Wetmore's bedroom at Chateau-sur-Mer. In the shape of superimposed tea trays, the faux bamboo turned and splayed feet and the finish of its surface, the table is a highly artistic adaptation of traditional Japanese forms, and surfaces, for the English market. The "maki-e" lacquer techinque uses gold specks sprinkled from a tube that has a tiny screen cover so the specks create a ground design only in the top portion of the lacquered surface which is then brushed over with a translucent lacquer and polished.
